actionResultText:
Here's your **Derivative Intuition Explorer**! 🎉

---

### How to use it:

| Feature | What to do |
|---|---|
| 🔴 **Drag Point P** | Click and drag the red point left/right along the parabola $f(x) = x^2$ |
| 🟠 **Secant Line** | The orange line passes through **P** and **Q** — its slope is $\dfrac{f(x+\Delta x) - f(x)}{\Delta x}$ |
| 🟣 **Tangent Line** | The purple line shows the true derivative $f'(x) = 2x$ at point P |
| 🎚️ **Δx Slider** | Drag it toward 0 — watch the secant rotate into the tangent |

---

### The Core Idea:

The derivative is defined as the **limit of the secant slope** as $\Delta x \to 0$:

$$f'(x) = \lim_{\Delta x \to 0} \frac{f(x + \Delta x) - f(x)}{\Delta x}$$

For $f(x) = x^2$, this gives $f'(x) = 2x$. As you shrink $\Delta x$ with the slider, the secant slope converges exactly to $2x$ — that's the geometric heart of the derivative!
